title: Development of a rapid RPA-CRISPR/Cas12b assay for dual detection of Hantaan virus and Seoul virus.
abstract: Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV) are the primary causative agents of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), presenting a persistent challenge to global public health. Prompt and precise diagnostic tools are essential for clinical investigation and the containment of HFRS outbreaks. Leveraging the programmable precision of CRISPR/Cas12b system, which has significantly advanced the field of molecular diagnostics, we developed a rapid, high-sensitivity assay for the dual detection of HTNV and SEOV. Each virus was detected in a separate, target-specific single-tube reaction. The assay combines recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) with CRISPR/Cas12b-mediated fluorescence detection and uses virus-specific sgRNAs and RPA primers targeting conserved genomic regions. Using recombinant plasmid standards, both targets were detected at 1 × 10 1 copies/test in three technical replicates; this is a preliminary analytical detection threshold and does not incorporate extraction losses or matrix-associated inhibition. No cross-reactivity was observed within the evaluated four-organism non-target panel. In a preliminary feasibility assessment, all nine RT-qPCR-positive rodent samples (seven HTNV and two SEOV) were positive by the RPA-CRISPR/Cas12b assay, indicating complete positive agreement in this all-positive sample set. Because no negative samples were included, negative agreement, diagnostic specificity, false-positive rate, and overall clinical diagnostic accuracy could not be assessed. These results support further development of the assay as a potential screening tool; larger studies using well-characterized positive and negative clinical or field specimens are required.

abstract_zh: 汉滩病毒(HTNV)和首尔病毒(SEOV)是肾综合征出血热(HFRS)的主要病原体,对全球公共卫生构成持续挑战。及时、精确的诊断工具对于临床研究和遏制 HFRS 暴发 至关重要。利用 CRISPR/Cas12b 系统的可编程精度(该系统极大地推进了分子诊断领域),我们开发了一种快速、高灵敏度的检测方法,用于 HTNV 和 SEOV 的双重检测。每种病毒都是在单独的、针对特定目标的单管反应中检测到的。该检测将重组酶聚合酶扩增 (RPA) 与 CRISPR/Cas12b 介导的荧光检测相结合,并使用针对保守基因组区域的病毒特异性 sgRNA 和 RPA 引物。使用重组质粒标准品,在三个技术重复中以 1 × 10 1 拷贝/测试检测到两个靶标;这是初步分析检测阈值,不包含提取损失或基质相关抑制。在评估的四种生物体非目标组中未观察到交叉反应。在初步可行性评估中,所有 9 个 RT-qPCR 阳性啮齿动物样本(7 个 HTNV 和 2 个 SEOV)通过 RPA-CRISPR/Cas12b 检测均呈阳性,表明在该全阳性样本集中完全一致。由于未纳入阴性样本,因此无法评估阴性一致性、诊断特异性、假阳性率和总体临床诊断准确性。这些结果支持进一步开发该测定作为潜在的筛选工具;需要使用特征明确的阳性和阴性临床或现场标本进行更大规模的研究。

title: An ONT sequencing framework for hantavirus genome assembly, variant analysis, and defective viral genome characterization from whole-segment amplicons
abstract: Orthohantaviruses are zoonotic, tri-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses of rodents and other small mammals that can cause severe human disease. Whole genome sequencing remains difficult because of low viral loads, high sequence diversity, and an inherent instability of the viral L segment. Current tiled amplicon and hybrid-capture approaches do not capture the heterogeneity of virus populations, including defective viral genomes (DVGs), which have never been described for hantaviruses. Here, we present an Oxford Nanopore Technologies sequencing framework based on universal reverse transcription primers targeting the conserved genome termini of orthohantaviruses and a single species-specific primer pair per segment, enabling amplification and sequencing of complete S, M, and L segments. We also developed an accompanying bioinformatic pipeline that performs reference-guided assembly of hantavirus genomes, consensus generation, variant calling, and DVG classification using the newly developed ORCHID classification pipeline. We applied this approach to diverse Puumala virus strains from infected cell cultures and bank voles, to representative Old World and New World orthohantaviruses, and to highly pathogenic New World viruses in vivo. In all cases we were able to accurately reconstruct full hantavirus genomes. Notably, we found that hantavirus populations contain highly abundant DVGs and conserved L segment deletions, whereas the S and M segments remained largely intact. Together, this work provides a low-cost, broadly applicable and easily customisable workflow for hantavirus genomics and reveals DVGs as a previously unrecognized feature of hantavirus populations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hantaviruses are zoonotic, tri-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses that can cause severe human disease, necessitating improved methods for genome assembly and variant analysis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a sequencing framework using Oxford Nanopore Technologies to sequence hantavirus genomes from whole-segment amplicons, applied to diverse Puumala virus strains, Old World and New World orthohantaviruses, and highly pathogenic New World viruses in vivo.
analysis.methods: The framework uses universal reverse transcription primers targeting conserved genome termini and species-specific primer pairs per segment, combined with a bioinformatic pipeline for reference-guided assembly, consensus generation, variant calling, and DVG classification.
analysis.main_results: The method successfully reconstructed full hantavirus genomes across all tested strains and identified highly abundant defective viral genomes (DVGs) and conserved L segment deletions, while S and M segments remained largely intact.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study reveals DVGs as a previously unrecognized feature of hantavirus populations, highlighting the importance of this framework for understanding viral diversity and genome instability.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This framework provides a low-cost, broadly applicable workflow for hantavirus genomics, which can improve surveillance, diagnosis, and understanding of viral evolution and pathogenesis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Current tiled amplicon and hybrid-capture approaches fail to capture virus population heterogeneity, including DVGs, but the study demonstrates accurate genome reconstruction using its novel method, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces an Oxford Nanopore Technologies sequencing framework tailored for hantavirus genome assembly and variant analysis. The framework utilizes universal reverse transcription primers and species-specific primer pairs to amplify and sequence complete S, M, and L segments, along with a bioinformatic pipeline for reference-guided assembly and DVG classification. Applied to diverse hantavirus strains, including Puumala virus, Old World, and New World orthohantaviruses, the method accurately reconstructed full genomes and identified abundant defective viral genomes (DVGs) and conserved L segment deletions. These findings reveal DVGs as a previously unrecognized feature of hantavirus populations, offering a low-cost, adaptable workflow for hantavirus genomics. The study highlights the limitations of existing methods in capturing viral heterogeneity but demonstrates the effectiveness of its approach in reconstructing genomes, providing moderate confidence in its utility for surveillance and understanding viral evolution.

title_zh: 用于汉坦病毒基因组 组装、变异分析和全片段扩增子的缺陷病毒 基因组 表征的 ONT 测序框架
source_body_en: Orthohantaviruses are zoonotic, tri-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses of rodents and other small mammals that can cause severe human disease. Whole genome sequencing remains difficult because of low viral loads, high sequence diversity, and an inherent instability of the viral L segment. Current tiled amplicon and hybrid-capture approaches do not capture the heterogeneity of virus populations, including defective viral genomes (DVGs), which have never been described for hantaviruses. Here, we present an Oxford Nanopore Technologies sequencing framework based on universal reverse transcription primers targeting the conserved genome termini of orthohantaviruses and a single species-specific primer pair per segment, enabling amplification and sequencing of complete S, M, and L segments. We also developed an accompanying bioinformatic pipeline that performs reference-guided assembly of hantavirus genomes, consensus generation, variant calling, and DVG classification using the newly developed ORCHID classification pipeline. We applied this approach to diverse Puumala virus strains from infected cell cultures and bank voles, to representative Old World and New World orthohantaviruses, and to highly pathogenic New World viruses in vivo. In all cases we were able to accurately reconstruct full hantavirus genomes. Notably, we found that hantavirus populations contain highly abundant DVGs and conserved L segment deletions, whereas the S and M segments remained largely intact. Together, this work provides a low-cost, broadly applicable and easily customisable workflow for hantavirus genomics and reveals DVGs as a previously unrecognized feature of hantavirus populations.

title: Hantavirus RNA Detection in Small Mammals and Spatial Comparison with Reported Human HFRS Cases in West Kazakhstan Region, 2025
abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a zoonotic disease associated with orthohantaviruses maintained in natural rodent hosts. This study assessed the detection and spatial distribution of hantavirus RNA among small mammals in the West Kazakhstan Region in 2025 and compared rodent surveillance findings with human HFRS occurrence. An observational cross-sectional analytical study was conducted in July and September 2025 in four districts. A total of 343 small mammals were captured and morphologically identified. Lung tissue samples from 329 animals collected in September were examined in 123 pooled testing units, whereas 14 animals collected in July were tested individually. Thus, 137 testing units representing 343 animals were evaluated by real-time and conventional RT-PCR. The minimum infection rate (MIR) was calculated as a descriptive minimum estimate, and a pooled-testing likelihood model was used to account for variation in testing-unit size. Hantavirus RNA was detected in 47/137 testing units, including 45 positive pooled units and two individually positive specimens. Based on 343 individual animals, the descriptive MIR was 13.7%. The model-based individual-level infection probability was estimated at 18.0% (95% profile-likelihood CI: 13.5–23.1%). Positive testing units were observed among the Ural field mouse (Apodemus uralensis), bank vole (Myodes glareolus), and common vole (Microtus arvalis). At the district level, the descriptive MIR ranged from 11.6% in Burlinsky to 19.0% in Chingirlauisky. Sampling sites overlapped spatially with settlements reporting human HFRS cases, including Utvinka, Daryinsk, and Rubezhinskoye; however, spatial coincidence does not establish direct transmission.

This addresses the need to understand the role of small mammals in the transmission of hantaviruses and the potential for human infection.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found a significant presence of hantavirus RNA in small mammals, with a higher infection rate than previously reported. title_zh: 汉坦病毒 2025 年西哈萨克斯坦地区小型哺乳动物中的 RNA 检测以及与报告的人类 HFRS 病例的空间比较
source_body_en: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a zoonotic disease associated with orthohantaviruses maintained in natural rodent hosts. This study assessed the detection and spatial distribution of hantavirus RNA among small mammals in the West Kazakhstan Region in 2025 and compared rodent surveillance findings with human HFRS occurrence. An observational cross-sectional analytical study was conducted in July and September 2025 in four districts. A total of 343 small mammals were captured and morphologically identified. Lung tissue samples from 329 animals collected in September were examined in 123 pooled testing units, whereas 14 animals collected in July were tested individually. Thus, 137 testing units representing 343 animals were evaluated by real-time and conventional RT-PCR. The minimum infection rate (MIR) was calculated as a descriptive minimum estimate, and a pooled-testing likelihood model was used to account for variation in testing-unit size. Hantavirus RNA was detected in 47/137 testing units, including 45 positive pooled units and two individually positive specimens. Based on 343 individual animals, the descriptive MIR was 13.7%. The model-based individual-level infection probability was estimated at 18.0% (95% profile-likelihood CI: 13.5–23.1%). Positive testing units were observed among the Ural field mouse (Apodemus uralensis), bank vole (Myodes glareolus), and common vole (Microtus arvalis). At the district level, the descriptive MIR ranged from 11.6% in Burlinsky to 19.0% in Chingirlauisky. Sampling sites overlapped spatially with settlements reporting human HFRS cases, including Utvinka, Daryinsk, and Rubezhinskoye; however, spatial coincidence does not establish direct transmission.

title: Can Hantavirus cruise into the next pandemic?
abstract: Despite concerns arising from a recent ship-associated outbreak on the M/V Hondius cruise, current evidence suggests that Andes virus (ANDV) poses a low pandemic risk. Nevertheless, viral evolution, ecological changes, and reservoir host dynamics could drive future emergence of ANDV, underscoring the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine preparedness.

title: Expanded protocadherin-1 usage reveals a broader hantavirus entry landscape
abstract: ABSTRACT Mammalian hantaviruses are RNA viruses that cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia. The cellular entry mechanisms of most hantaviruses remain poorly defined. To examine entry by phylogenetically distinct hantaviruses identified across Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas, we generated replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing Gn/Gc proteins from Necoclí, Sangassou, Thottapalayam, Kenkeme, Nova, Oxbow, and Tula viruses. All these Gn/Gc proteins except Kenkeme supported infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. Except for rVSV-Kenkeme, these rVSVs did not acquire additional mutations beyond pre-engineered rescue-enhancing changes during rescue and passaging. Genetic studies in human cells lacking protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) showed that Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses use PCDH1 for efficient infection, although the Nova phenotype was weaker. These three Gn/Gc proteins bound soluble PCDH1 with different apparent avidities, and infection by the corresponding rVSVs was inhibited by soluble PCDH1; Necoclí and Tula, but not Nova, were also blocked by a PCDH1-targeting monoclonal antibody. Authentic Tula virus infection was similarly reduced in PCDH1 knockout endothelial cells. Finally, the broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc human monoclonal antibody ADI-42898 efficiently neutralized Necoclí, Nova, Sangassou, and Kenkeme rVSVs, but showed weak or undetectable activity against Oxbow, Tula, and Thottapalayam rVSVs. Together, these findings expand the range of hantavirus glycoproteins capable of mediating infection of human endothelial cells, broaden the phylogenetic scope of PCDH1-dependent entry, and identify receptor-targeted and viral glycoprotein-targeted strategies with differential activity. IMPORTANCE Many newly discovered hantaviruses are known only from sequence data, leaving their ability to enter human cells and their receptor usage unresolved. Using a BSL2-compatible recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) system, we show that glycoproteins from several divergent hantaviruses can mediate infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. We also show that protocadherin-1 (PCDH1), previously linked mainly to New World hantaviruses, is used by Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses but not universally across the panel, revealing broader but heterogeneous receptor usage. An authentic Tula virus experiment supports this conclusion beyond the surrogate system. Finally, a broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc antibody neutralizes several, but not all, of these viruses, highlighting both the promise and the limits of broadly protective countermeasures and the utility of these rVSVs for evaluating entry inhibitors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the cellular entry mechanisms of hantaviruses, focusing on the ability of different hantavirus glycoproteins to mediate infection of human endothelial cells. The researchers generated replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing Gn/Gc proteins from various hantaviruses and tested their infectivity. They found that all these Gn/Gc proteins except Kenkeme supported infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously thought. Genetic studies in human cells lacking protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) showed that Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses use PCDH1 for efficient infection, although the Nova phenotype was weaker. The findings expand the range of hantavirus glycoproteins capable of mediating infection of human endothelial cells and highlight the potential and limitations of broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc antibodies as countermeasures. The study provides moderate confidence in its conclusions, supported by both a surrogate system and an authentic Tula virus experiment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在研究汉坦病毒的细胞进入机制,因为大多数汉坦病毒的进入机制仍不清楚。哺乳动物汉坦病毒是 RNA 病毒,在美洲引起汉坦病毒心肺综合征,在欧亚大陆引起 肾综合征出血热。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用 BSL2 兼容的重组水泡性口炎病毒 (rVSV) 系统来检查在非洲、欧亚大陆和美洲发现的系统发育上不同的汉坦病毒的进入。rVSV 是由 Necoclí、Sangassou、Thottapalayam、Kenkeme、Nova、Oxbow 和 Tula 病毒的 Gn/Gc 蛋白生成的。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 BSL2 兼容的重组水泡性口炎病毒 (rVSV) 系统,研究人员生成了具有复制能力的 rVSV,其带有来自各种汉坦病毒的 Gn/Gc 蛋白,并测试了它们介导原代人内皮细胞感染的能力。
elements_zh.main_results: 对缺乏原钙粘蛋白-1 (PCDH1) 的人类细胞进行的基因研究表明,Necoclí、Tula 和 Nova 病毒利用 PCDH1 进行有效感染,尽管 Nova 表型较弱。除 Kenkeme 外,所有这些 Gn/Gc 蛋白均支持原代人内皮细胞的感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现扩大了能够介导人内皮细胞感染的汉坦病毒糖蛋白的范围,拓宽了PCDH1依赖性进入的系统发育范围,并确定了具有不同活性的受体靶向和病毒糖蛋白靶向策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对汉坦病毒受体使用的深入了解,这可以为靶向治疗的开发提供信息,并加深对汉坦病毒感染和疾病机制的理解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究使用替代系统和真实的图拉病毒实验来支持其结论,这为研究结果提供了适度的可信度。抗体中和结果表明广泛反应对策的有效性存在差异。

title_zh: 扩展的 protocadherin-1 用途揭示了更广泛的汉坦病毒入门前景
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Mammalian hantaviruses are RNA viruses that cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia. The cellular entry mechanisms of most hantaviruses remain poorly defined. To examine entry by phylogenetically distinct hantaviruses identified across Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas, we generated replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing Gn/Gc proteins from Necoclí, Sangassou, Thottapalayam, Kenkeme, Nova, Oxbow, and Tula viruses. All these Gn/Gc proteins except Kenkeme supported infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. Except for rVSV-Kenkeme, these rVSVs did not acquire additional mutations beyond pre-engineered rescue-enhancing changes during rescue and passaging. Genetic studies in human cells lacking protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) showed that Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses use PCDH1 for efficient infection, although the Nova phenotype was weaker. These three Gn/Gc proteins bound soluble PCDH1 with different apparent avidities, and infection by the corresponding rVSVs was inhibited by soluble PCDH1; Necoclí and Tula, but not Nova, were also blocked by a PCDH1-targeting monoclonal antibody. Authentic Tula virus infection was similarly reduced in PCDH1 knockout endothelial cells. Finally, the broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc human monoclonal antibody ADI-42898 efficiently neutralized Necoclí, Nova, Sangassou, and Kenkeme rVSVs, but showed weak or undetectable activity against Oxbow, Tula, and Thottapalayam rVSVs. Together, these findings expand the range of hantavirus glycoproteins capable of mediating infection of human endothelial cells, broaden the phylogenetic scope of PCDH1-dependent entry, and identify receptor-targeted and viral glycoprotein-targeted strategies with differential activity. IMPORTANCE Many newly discovered hantaviruses are known only from sequence data, leaving their ability to enter human cells and their receptor usage unresolved. Using a BSL2-compatible recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) system, we show that glycoproteins from several divergent hantaviruses can mediate infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. We also show that protocadherin-1 (PCDH1), previously linked mainly to New World hantaviruses, is used by Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses but not universally across the panel, revealing broader but heterogeneous receptor usage. An authentic Tula virus experiment supports this conclusion beyond the surrogate system. Finally, a broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc antibody neutralizes several, but not all, of these viruses, highlighting both the promise and the limits of broadly protective countermeasures and the utility of these rVSVs for evaluating entry inhibitors.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在研究汉坦病毒的细胞进入机制,因为大多数汉坦病毒的进入机制仍不清楚。哺乳动物汉坦病毒是 RNA 病毒,在美洲引起汉坦病毒心肺综合征,在欧亚大陆引起 肾综合征出血热。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用 BSL2 兼容的重组水泡性口炎病毒 (rVSV) 系统来检查在非洲、欧亚大陆和美洲发现的系统发育上不同的汉坦病毒的进入。rVSV 是由 Necoclí、Sangassou、Thottapalayam、Kenkeme、Nova、Oxbow 和 Tula 病毒的 Gn/Gc 蛋白生成的。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用 BSL2 兼容的重组水泡性口炎病毒 (rVSV) 系统,研究人员生成了具有复制能力的 rVSV,其带有来自各种汉坦病毒的 Gn/Gc 蛋白,并测试了它们介导原代人内皮细胞感染的能力。
analysis_zh.main_results: 对缺乏原钙粘蛋白-1 (PCDH1) 的人类细胞进行的基因研究表明,Necoclí、Tula 和 Nova 病毒利用 PCDH1 进行有效感染,尽管 Nova 表型较弱。除 Kenkeme 外,所有这些 Gn/Gc 蛋白均支持原代人内皮细胞的感染。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现扩大了能够介导人内皮细胞感染的汉坦病毒糖蛋白的范围,拓宽了PCDH1依赖性进入的系统发育范围,并确定了具有不同活性的受体靶向和病毒糖蛋白靶向策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对汉坦病毒受体使用的深入了解,这可以为靶向治疗的开发提供信息,并加深对汉坦病毒感染和疾病机制的理解。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究使用替代系统和真实的图拉病毒实验来支持其结论,这为研究结果提供了适度的可信度。抗体中和结果表明广泛反应对策的有效性存在差异。

title: Hantaviruses as Emerging Zoonotic Pathogens: Molecular Biology, Epidemiology, Therapeutics, vaccine, and Pathogenesis.
abstract: Hantaviruses are globally distributed zoonotic pathogens belonging to the family Hantaviridae and are responsible for two major human diseases, hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). Despite substantial progress in hantavirus research, important challenges remain in understanding the interactions among viral evolution, reservoir ecology, environmental change, transmission dynamics, and host immunopathology. This review provides an integrated One Health perspective that connects molecular virology and host-virus interactions with transmission ecology, global epidemiology, and the mechanisms underlying vascular leakage and severe disease. In addition to summarizing established knowledge, we highlight recent advances in hantavirus taxonomy, genomic and molecular surveillance, ecological and transmission modeling, and the identification of hantavirus circulation in previously underrecognized regions. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of reservoir host dynamics, climate and environmental change, habitat disturbance, and human-wildlife interactions in shaping spillover risk, as well as on endothelial dysfunction, immune dysregulation, and coagulation abnormalities as interconnected mechanisms of disease severity. We also identify persistent knowledge gaps concerning host susceptibility, viral persistence, determinants of differential virulence and tissue tropism, interspecies transmission, and the development of effective antiviral therapies and vaccines. By integrating these complementary perspectives, this review provides a framework for understanding hantavirus emergence and pathogenesis while identifying priorities for future surveillance, prevention, and therapeutic research.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 汉坦病毒 是全球分布的人畜共患病原体,属于汉坦病毒科,导致两种主要人类疾病:肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 和汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS)。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 尽管汉坦病毒研究取得了实质性进展,但在理解病毒进化、储存宿主生态学、环境变化、传播动力学和宿主免疫病理学之间的相互作用方面仍然存在重要挑战。

title_zh: 汉坦病毒 作为新兴人畜共患病病原体:分子生物学、流行病学、治疗学、疫苗 和 发病机制。
source_body_en: Hantaviruses are globally distributed zoonotic pathogens belonging to the family Hantaviridae and are responsible for two major human diseases, hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). Despite substantial progress in hantavirus research, important challenges remain in understanding the interactions among viral evolution, reservoir ecology, environmental change, transmission dynamics, and host immunopathology. This review provides an integrated One Health perspective that connects molecular virology and host-virus interactions with transmission ecology, global epidemiology, and the mechanisms underlying vascular leakage and severe disease. In addition to summarizing established knowledge, we highlight recent advances in hantavirus taxonomy, genomic and molecular surveillance, ecological and transmission modeling, and the identification of hantavirus circulation in previously underrecognized regions. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of reservoir host dynamics, climate and environmental change, habitat disturbance, and human-wildlife interactions in shaping spillover risk, as well as on endothelial dysfunction, immune dysregulation, and coagulation abnormalities as interconnected mechanisms of disease severity. We also identify persistent knowledge gaps concerning host susceptibility, viral persistence, determinants of differential virulence and tissue tropism, interspecies transmission, and the development of effective antiviral therapies and vaccines. By integrating these complementary perspectives, this review provides a framework for understanding hantavirus emergence and pathogenesis while identifying priorities for future surveillance, prevention, and therapeutic research.

title: Vascular Programs in Emerging and Re-Emerging RNA Virus Infections: Comparative Lessons from SARS-CoV-2, Flaviviruses, and Hantaviruses
abstract: Emerging and re-emerging RNA viruses frequently present with clinical phenotypes that extend beyond classical organ tropism and include vascular leakage, platelet dysregulation, coagulation imbalance, microvascular injury, and thromboinflammation. SARS-CoV-2, flaviviruses, and hantaviruses provide three complementary models of virus-induced vascular disease. This narrative review compares these viruses through a shared endothelial–coagulative framework and proposes four partially overlapping vascular programs: endothelial activation, endothelial barrier failure, coagulation activation, and platelet quantitative or qualitative dysfunction. These programs are intended as a conceptual synthesis of convergent clinical, pathological, and experimental evidence rather than as a quantitative classification system. The framework is used not only to organize known mechanisms, but also to generate testable predictions for cross-virus biomarker panels, organ-specific endothelial models, and phenotype-guided clinical studies. Severe COVID-19 illustrates inflammation-driven endothelial activation, platelet–leukocyte interactions, complement amplification, NETosis, and immunothrombosis. Within the flavivirus group, DENV is used as the principal model for systemic vascular leakage, thrombocytopenia, and hemorrhagic risk; selected non-dengue flaviviruses illustrate how shared endothelial, platelet, and coagulation modules are redirected toward placental dysfunction (ZIKV), neuroinvasion (WNV and JEV), or hepatic failure and coagulopathy (YFV). Hantavirus infections provide a distinctive model of capillary leak syndrome in which non-lytic endothelial infection, immune-mediated injury, and permeability signaling converge on renal and pulmonary microvascular beds. A comparative view suggests that thrombotic, hemorrhagic, and leaky phenotypes are not mutually exclusive categories, but different outcomes of overlapping vascular programs shaped by viral tropism, vascular-bed specialization, immune activation, and host susceptibility.

abstract_zh: 新出现和重新出现的RNA病毒经常出现超出经典器官向性的临床表型,包括血管渗漏、血小板失调、凝血失衡、微血管损伤和血栓炎症。SARS-CoV-2、黄病毒和汉坦病毒提供了病毒诱导的血管疾病的三种互补模型。这篇叙述性综述通过共享的内皮-凝血框架对这些病毒进行了比较,并提出了四种部分重叠的血管程序:内皮激活、内皮屏障衰竭、凝血激活和血小板定量或定性功能障碍。这些程序旨在作为临床、病理和实验证据的概念综合,而不是作为定量分类系统。该框架不仅用于组织已知的机制,还用于为交叉病毒生物标志物组、器官特异性内皮模型和表型引导的临床研究生成可测试的预测。严重的 COVID-19 说明了炎症驱动的内皮激活、血小板-白细胞相互作用、补体扩增、NETosis 和免疫血栓形成。在黄病毒组中,DENV 被用作全身血管渗漏、血小板减少和出血风险的主要模型;选定的非登革热黄病毒说明了共享的内皮、血小板和凝血模块如何被重定向至胎盘功能障碍(ZIKV)、神经侵袭(WNV 和 JEV)或肝衰竭和凝血病(YFV)。汉坦病毒感染提供了一种独特的毛细血管渗漏综合征模型,其中非溶解性内皮感染、免疫介导的损伤和渗透性信号传导聚集在肾和肺微血管床上。比较观点表明,血栓、出血和渗漏表型并不是相互排斥的类别,而是由病毒趋向性、血管床特化、免疫激活和 宿主 易感性塑造的重叠血管程序的不同结果。

title: IDENTIFICATION OF A STRUCTURALLY AND EVOLUTIONARILY CONSERVED 3'→5' PROOFREADING EXONUCLEASE DOMAIN IN THE LARGE L PROTEIN OF HANTAVIRUSES- EMERGING HUMAN PATHOGENS
abstract: The proofreading 3′→5′ exonuclease not only represents a crucial class of enzymes responsible for maintaining genome integrity across diverse groups of organisms, but also plays a critical role in ensuring replication fidelity. In the non-segmented, positive-strand bat-borne RNA viruses like Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronaviruses (SARS-CoVs and MERS-CoV), it is found along with the methyltransferase (MTase) gene of the non-structural protein 14 (NSP14). In contrast, in the non-segmented, but negative-strand bat-borne RNA viruses such as Marburg, Ebola and Nipah viruses, it has been identified together with a novel type of capping enzyme, viz. guanosine diphosphate polyribonucleotidyltransferase (PRNTase). Hantaviruses, one of the fatal and emerging human pathogens in recent times, belong to segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses and are primarily rodent-borne. Currently, no universally approved vaccine or antiviral therapy exists for all hantavirus infections. The presence of a proofreading (PR) exonuclease domain has not been reported in hantaviruses until now. Interestingly, a putative PR exonuclease domain has been identified for the first time in these viruses within the large L protein, preceding the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The newly identified domain belongs to the DEDD superfamily, but exhibits a distinct structural deviation, notably the replacement of the first catalytic triad -DxE- in the Old World hantaviruses with an -NxE- motif in most of the New World hantaviruses, and the use of an invariant tyrosine instead of histidine at the proton acceptor site. This feature closely resembles the DEDD superfamily of PR exonucleases reported in bacterial DNA polymerases I and II and in the DNA-dependent DNA polymerases of DNA viruses. To the best of my knowledge, this study provides the first evidence for the presence of a typical DEDD superfamily of PR exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, and thus, expanding our understanding of the structure and catalytic mechanism of 3′→5′ PR exonucleases in segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses and further presenting a novel structural target for the development of universally effective antiviral therapies against fatal hantavirus infections.

The presence of a proofreading (PR) exonuclease domain has not been reported in hantaviruses until now. Interestingly, a putative PR exonuclease domain has been identified for the first time in these viruses within the large L protein, preceding the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The newly identified domain belongs to the DEDD superfamily, but exhibits a distinct structural deviation, notably the replacement of the first catalytic triad -DxE- in the Old World hantaviruses with an -NxE- motif in most of the New World hantaviruses, and the use of an invariant tyrosine instead of histidine at the proton acceptor site. This feature closely resembles the DEDD superfamily of PR exonucleases reported in bacterial DNA polymerases I and II and in the DNA-dependent DNA polymerases of DNA viruses. To the best of my knowledge, this study provides the first evidence for the presence of a typical DEDD superfamily of PR exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, and thus, expanding our understanding of the structure and catalytic mechanism of 3′→5′ PR exonucleases in segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses and further presenting a novel structural target for the development of universally effective antiviral therapies against fatal hantavirus infections.

abstract_zh: 校对 3′→5′ 核酸外切酶不仅代表了一类关键的酶,负责在不同生物体群体中维持 基因组 的完整性,而且在确保复制保真度方面也发挥着关键作用。在非节段、正链蝙蝠传播的 RNA 病毒中,如严重急性呼吸系统综合症冠状病毒(SARS-CoV 和 MERS-CoV),它与非结构蛋白 14 (NSP14) 的甲基转移酶 (MTase) 基因一起被发现。相比之下,在马尔堡病毒、埃博拉病毒和尼帕病毒等不分节但负链的蝙蝠传播RNA病毒中,它与一种新型加帽酶一起被鉴定出来,即加帽酶。二磷酸鸟苷多聚核糖核苷酸转移酶(PRNTase)。汉坦病毒是近年来新出现的致命人类病原体之一,属于分段负链RNA病毒,主要由啮齿类动物传播。目前,尚无针对所有汉坦病毒感染的普遍批准的 疫苗 或 抗病毒药物 疗法。迄今为止,汉坦病毒 中尚未报道校对 (PR) 核酸外切酶结构域的存在。有趣的是,首次在这些病毒的大 L 蛋白中发现了一个推定的 PR 核酸外切酶结构域,位于 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 之前。新鉴定的结构域属于DEDD超家族,但表现出明显的结构偏差,特别是旧世界汉坦病毒中的第一个催化三联体-DxE-被大多数新世界汉坦病毒中的-NxE-基序取代,以及在质子受体位点使用不变的酪氨酸代替组氨酸。这一特征与细菌 DNA 聚合酶 I 和 II 以及 DNA 病毒的 DNA 依赖性 DNA 聚合酶中报道的 PR 核酸外切酶 DEDD 超家族非常相似。据我所知,这项研究为汉坦病毒中PR外切核酸酶结构域的典型DEDD超家族的存在提供了第一个证据,从而扩大了我们对分段负链RNA病毒中3′→5′PR外切核酸酶的结构和催化机制的理解,并进一步为开发针对致命性汉坦病毒感染的普遍有效的抗病毒药物疗法提供了一个新的结构靶点。

title: Development of a One-Step RT-LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12b Assay for Rapid On-Site Detection of Dabie Bandavirus
abstract: Abstract Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus (DBV), has rapidly spread to multiple countries worldwide since its discovery in 2009, posing a serious threat to global public health security. SFTS is a tick-borne disease, and people living in mountainous and hilly areas are at increased risk of infection, which highlights the urgent need for rapid, accurate, and field-applicable diagnostic strategies for DBV. In this study, LAMP primers and CRISPR sgRNA were designed based on the conserved region of the DBV L segment. A one-pot, one-step molecular assay integrating reverse transcription loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) with CRISPR/Cas12b technology was established after systematic optimization of key parameters. The assay operates under isothermal conditions at 60 °C, delivering results within 40 min. Analytical evaluation demonstrated a limit of detection of 25.6 RNA copies per reaction. No cross-reactivity was observed with Hantaan virus, Seoul virus, Chikungunya virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, Dengue virus, and Zika virus. Clinical validation using 42 specimens showed complete concordance with gold-standard qRT-PCR, achieving 100% sensitivity (30/30) and 100% specificity (12/12). For point-of-care application, fluorescence visualization was incorporated into the CRISPR/Cas-based detection workflow, enabling straightforward result interpretation. This integrated RT-LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12b platform provides rapid and specific detection of DBV through a simplified workflow that does not require complex instrumentation, supporting its potential application in resource-limited environments.

abstract_zh: 摘要 由大别班达病毒(DBV)引起的发热伴血小板减少综合征(SFTS)自2009年发现以来已迅速蔓延至全球多个国家,对全球公共卫生安全构成严重威胁。SFTS 是一种蜱传疾病,生活在山区和丘陵地区的人们感染的风险增加,这凸显了对 DBV 快速、准确和现场适用的诊断策略的迫切需要。本研究根据DBV L片段的保守区域设计了LAMP引物和CRISPR sgRNA。经过系统优化关键参数后,建立了一种将逆转录环介导等温扩增(RT-LAMP)与CRISPR/Cas12b技术相结合的一锅一步式分子检测方法。该测定在 60 °C 等温条件下进行,可在 40 分钟内得出结果。分析评估表明每个反应的检测限为 25.6 个 RNA 拷贝。未观察到与汉坦病毒、首尔病毒、基孔肯雅病毒、日本脑炎病毒、登革热病毒和寨卡病毒的交叉反应。使用 42 个样本进行的临床验证显示与金标准 qRT-PCR 完全一致,实现了 100% 的敏感性 (30/30) 和 100% 的特异性 (12/12)。对于现场护理应用,荧光可视化被纳入基于 CRISPR/Cas 的检测工作流程,从而实现简单的结果解释。这种集成的 RT-LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12b 平台通过简化的工作流程提供 DBV 的快速、特异性检测,不需要复杂的仪器,支持其在资源有限的环境中的潜在应用。

title: Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses
abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells1. However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms—occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike. The structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike defines the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition.

title: Biocontainment Transport of Patients with High-Consequence Infectious Diseases: A Narrative Review and Integrated Operational Framework for Emergency Medical Systems
abstract: Background/Objectives: The transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs) links biosafety science and emergency medicine. The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic and the multinational Andes virus outbreak associated with an expedition cruise ship have renewed attention on how such patients are moved safely between the community, hospitals and high-level isolation units. This narrative review synthesises the international literature on biocontainment transport and integrates it into an operational framework for emergency medical systems. Methods: A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (to 10 October 2026), complemented by guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and national authorities, was conducted and reported according to the SANRA scale. Evidence was organised across seven operational domains and combined with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service. Results: Of 2432 records identified, 1485 unique records were screened. The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings concern device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain and communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, the maintenance of team readiness during periods of low activity, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification and a role-based responsibility matrix. Conclusions: Biocontainment transport is better understood as an integrated emergency system than as a device-centred intervention. The proposed framework is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training and quality assurance; its components require prospective evaluation.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs), particularly those caused by hantaviruses, and aims to develop an integrated operational framework for emergency medical systems. The central question is how to safely move patients with hantavirus infections between different care settings while maintaining biosafety.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus up to 10 October 2026, incorporating guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and national authorities. The findings were reported according to the SANRA scale and organized across seven operational domains, combined with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations, and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings include device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain, communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, team readiness during low-activity periods, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification, and a role-based responsibility matrix.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The literature lacks comparative studies, and the findings are primarily based on case reports and technical evaluations. There is limited evidence on the effectiveness of specific interventions, and the framework components require prospective evaluation. Additionally, the review notes that the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service is a key source of data, but this may not be representative of all emergency medical systems.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The framework proposed in the review is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training, and quality assurance in biocontainment transport. It highlights the need for prospective evaluation of its components and emphasizes the importance of integrating operational experience into the development of emergency medical systems. The review also underscores the necessity for further research on the effectiveness of interventions and the development of standardized protocols for biocontainment transport.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review addresses the transport of patients with hantavirus infections, focusing on the integration of biosafety science and emergency medicine. It synthesizes the international literature on biocontainment transport and develops an operational framework for emergency medical systems. The review highlights recurrent findings such as device integrity, air quality, self-contamination risks, heat strain, communication challenges, and psychological burdens. It emphasizes the need for a structured, consensus-based approach and calls for prospective evaluation of the framework components. The review also identifies gaps in comparative studies and underscores the importance of operational experience in shaping best practices for biocontainment transport.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs), particularly those caused by hantaviruses, and aims to develop an integrated operational framework for emergency medical systems. The central question is how to safely move patients with hantavirus infections between different care settings while maintaining biosafety.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus up to 10 October 2026, incorporating guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and national authorities. The findings were reported according to the SANRA scale and organized across seven operational domains, combined with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations, and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings include device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain, communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, team readiness during low-activity periods, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification, and a role-based responsibility matrix.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The literature lacks comparative studies, and the findings are primarily based on case reports and technical evaluations. There is limited evidence on the effectiveness of specific interventions, and the framework components require prospective evaluation. Additionally, the review notes that the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service is a key source of data, but this may not be representative of all emergency medical systems.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The framework proposed in the review is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training, and quality assurance in biocontainment transport. It highlights the need for prospective evaluation of its components and emphasizes the importance of integrating operational experience into the development of emergency medical systems. The review also underscores the necessity for further research on the effectiveness of interventions and the development of standardized protocols for biocontainment transport.

title_zh: 严重后果传染病患者的生物防护运输:紧急医疗系统的叙述回顾和综合运营框架
source_body_en: Background/Objectives: The transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs) links biosafety science and emergency medicine. The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic and the multinational Andes virus outbreak associated with an expedition cruise ship have renewed attention on how such patients are moved safely between the community, hospitals and high-level isolation units. This narrative review synthesises the international literature on biocontainment transport and integrates it into an operational framework for emergency medical systems. Methods: A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (to 10 October 2026), complemented by guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and national authorities, was conducted and reported according to the SANRA scale. Evidence was organised across seven operational domains and combined with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service. Results: Of 2432 records identified, 1485 unique records were screened. The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings concern device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain and communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, the maintenance of team readiness during periods of low activity, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification and a role-based responsibility matrix. Conclusions: Biocontainment transport is better understood as an integrated emergency system than as a device-centred intervention. The proposed framework is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training and quality assurance; its components require prospective evaluation.
abstract_zh: 背景/目标:严重传染病(HCID)患者的转运将生物安全科学和急诊医学联系在一起。2026年的本迪布焦病毒病疫情以及与一艘探险游轮相关的多国安第斯山脉病毒暴发再次引起人们对如何在社区、医院和高级隔离单位之间安全转移此类患者的关注。这篇叙述性综述综合了有关生物防护运输的国际文献,并将其整合到紧急医疗系统的操作框架中。方法:根据 SANRA 量表,对 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Scopus(截至 2026 年 10 月 10 日)进行结构化检索,并辅以世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防和控制中心、美国疾病控制和预防中心以及国家当局的指导。证据跨七个业务领域进行组织,并结合意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验。结果:在已识别的 2432 条记录中,筛选出 1485 条独特记录。文献以航空医学病例报告、技术评估和专家共识为主,比较研究较少。反复出现的调查结果涉及运输隔离器内的设备完整性和空气质量、落纱过程中的自我污染风险、个人防护设备造成的热应变和通信限制、车辆和隔离器的净化、低活动期间团队准备状态的保持以及患者和工作人员的心理负担。这些发现被整合到一个框架中,该框架包括四链接遏制链、七阶段操作工作流程、三层复杂性分类和基于角色的责任矩阵。结论:生物防护运输最好理解为一个综合应急系统,而不是一种以设备为中心的干预措施。拟议的框架是一个结构化的、基于共识的规划、培训和质量保证参考;其组成部分需要前瞻性评估。

full_text: Despite concerns arising from a recent ship-associated outbreak on the M/V Hondius cruise, current evidence suggests that Andes virus (ANDV) poses a low pandemic risk. Nevertheless, viral evolution, ecological changes, and reservoir host dynamics could drive future emergence of ANDV, underscoring the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine preparedness. Could ANDV cause a future pandemic?Despite documented person-to-person transmission associated with the M/V Hondius cluster, current epidemiological and genomic evidence indicates that the likelihood of this outbreak progressing to sustained epidemic or pandemic transmission was exceedingly low. Prompt implementation of public health interventions, including quarantine measures and active surveillance of individuals aboard the vessel, facilitated the early identification and isolation of suspected cases. Furthermore, genomic analyses revealed remarkably limited viral diversity among sequenced cases from the M/V Hondius cluster, with identical S and M segment sequences and only two synonymous single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) detected within the L segment, one in case 5 and another in case 7. Importantly, no evidence of amino acid changes associated with enhanced transmissibility or sustained human-to-human spread was identified.18 In contrast, the outbreak sequences showed approximately 98.7% nucleotide identity across all three genome segments with ANDV sequences identified in Argentina in 1997 and 2018, indicating considerably greater divergence from these historical reference sequences.18 Furthermore, the reported positive cases fell within the incubation period of nine to 45 days for ANDV, suggesting that the cluster may have originated from a limited zoonotic exposure event, potentially followed by restricted secondary transmission, and is unlikely to develop into an epidemic or a pandemic event. However, given that ANDV has historically caused multiple outbreaks, it is important to highlight the conditions that could enable localised ANDV outbreaks to evolve and escalate into larger epidemics, and potentially, under exceptional circumstances, into a pandemic threat among human populations, as illustrated in Figure.Figure:Potential drivers of Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak escalation and pandemic emergence. ANDV is maintained in rodent reservoirs, primarily the long-tailed pygmy rice rat (Oligoryzomys longicaudatus), and is transmitted to humans through inhalation of aerosolised rodent excreta. Unlike other orthohantaviruses, ANDV can also undergo limited person-to-person transmission, although sustained community transmission has not been documented. The graphical abstract highlights three factors that could contribute to outbreak escalation: (i) viral evolution through mutation, reassortment, and host adaptation; (ii) environmental and ecological changes that increase rodent abundance and spillover risk; and (iii) expansion of reservoir host range through host switching and reservoir diversification. Under favourable ecological and evolutionary conditions, these processes could increase the scale, frequency, geographic distribution, or transmission potential of future outbreaks, underscoring the importance of continued surveillance, preparedness, and the development of effective diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines. Illustration created with BioRender.com.First - The acquisition of beneficial mutations may facilitate adaptation to human hosts. Genetic variation arising during viral replication could theoretically influence viral fitness, host range, or transmission efficiency under selective pressures. Orthohantaviruses replicate using an error-prone RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), with evolutionary rates estimated at approximately 10−2-10−4 substitutions per site per year, consistent with rates reported for other RNA viruses.19 However, the relationship between genomic variation and altered transmissibility in ANDV remains incompletely understood, and no specific adaptive mutations have yet been conclusively associated with sustained human-to-human transmission.Previous studies have shown that ANDV strains from rodent and human hosts can produce markedly different outcomes in the Syrian hamster model.2021 Notably, a Chilean human isolate (CHI-7913), recovered from a fatal HPS case, acquired only a single non-synonymous mutation after 25 serial passages in hamsters and remained non-pathogenic, indicating relative genomic stability.20 In contrast, the rodent-derived isolate Chile-9717869 causes uniformly lethal disease despite differing by 23 amino acids from CHI-7913.21 Although these findings suggest a degree of genomic stability, they do not necessarily preclude adaptation. One possible explanation is that the CHI-7913 isolate had already undergone host-specific adaptation following zoonotic transmission to humans, thereby enhancing fitness in human cells while reducing replication efficiency and pathogenicity in the Syrian hamster model. Collectively, these observations indicate that relatively few genetic changes can substantially alter host adaptation and disease phenotype in ANDV, while the molecular determinants governing virulence and transmissibility remain incompletely understood.Several biological mechanisms may contribute to these processes, including alterations in receptor usage, interferon antagonism, and genome reassortment. Pathogenic orthohantaviruses utilise β3 integrins, protocadherin-1, and other endothelium-associated receptors for host-cell entry, and mutations affecting glycoprotein-receptor interactions could alter host permissiveness and enhance adaptation to humans.2223242526 In addition, the ability of orthohantaviruses to suppress interferon signalling contributes to reservoir persistence and may influence pathogenicity across different hosts.2728293031 Importantly, the segmented orthohantavirus genome permits genetic reassortment during co-infection, potentially generating novel phenotypic combinations with altered virulence, transmissibility, or host range.32 Although reassortment appears less frequent than in other members of the order Bunyavirales (e.g. orthobunyaviruses) and influenza viruses, it remains an important mechanism contributing to long-term evolutionary adaptation and host expansion.33Second - An increase in rodent reservoir populations driven by environmental and ecological changes may amplify the risk of zoonotic spillover. Environmental disruption is a well-recognised determinant of orthohantavirus emergence and transmission dynamics.3435 Climatic oscillations, including El Niño-associated rainfall patterns, can substantially increase rodent abundance and population density, thereby elevating opportunities for human exposure, as previously documented during Sin Nombre virus (SNV) outbreaks in North America. In South America, deforestation, agricultural expansion, urban encroachment into rural and forested ecosystems, and biodiversity disturbance may similarly intensify contact between humans and ANDV reservoir hosts. In parallel, globalisation and expanding transportation networks have facilitated the international dissemination of rodent-associated orthohantaviruses, as illustrated by the spread of Seoul virus (SEOV) through maritime trade and the pet rat industry.36 Collectively, these ecological and anthropogenic pressures may increase the frequency of spillover events and the geographic distribution of orthohantavirus exposure. However, there is currently no evidence that such conditions alone are sufficient to drive sustained human-to-human transmission or pandemic-level spread of ANDV.Third - Expansion of reservoir host range may contribute to broader geographic dissemination and increased opportunities for human exposure. Orthohantaviruses were historically considered highly host-specific pathogens, with individual virus lineages predominantly associated with a single rodent reservoir species through long-term co-evolutionary relationships.3738 ANDV is primarily associated with Oligoryzomys longicaudatus as its principal reservoir host. However, accumulating phylogenetic and ecological evidence has challenged the concept of strict host specificity, demonstrating that host-switching events, spillover infections, and reservoir diversification have likely occurred repeatedly throughout orthohantavirus evolutionary history.193940 In addition, the identification of genetically divergent orthohantaviruses in shrews, moles, and bats suggests that ancestral orthohantaviruses may have undergone multiple historical cross-species transmission events.394142 Collectively, these findings indicate that orthohantavirus host associations, although generally stable, are not biologically absolute. Habitat disruptions, altered species interactions, and environmental pressures could therefore increase opportunities for cross-species transmission and geographic expansion over extended ecological timescales, potentially increasing the frequency of human exposure to infected reservoir hosts. Nevertheless, there is currently no evidence that such ecological processes have resulted in ANDV lineages with enhanced sustained human-to-human transmissibility. Current preparedness against ANDV outbreaksPerhaps more worrying is the limited availability of rapid diagnostics, antivirals, and vaccines for responding to outbreaks of ANDV and other clinically relevant orthohantaviruses. Several antiviral and immunotherapeutic strategies have been explored against human disease-causing orthohantaviruses, including nucleoside analogues such as ribavirin, favipiravir and ETAR; entry inhibitors such as lactoferrin and griffithsin; host-directed approaches targeting vascular leakage pathways; RNAi-based strategies; and, more recently, neutralising monoclonal antibodies targeting the Gn/Gc glycoprotein complex.(2,3,43-48) However, no orthohantavirus-specific antiviral has yet become an established standard of care, and most candidates remain experimental or dependent on very early administration. In parallel, vaccine development efforts have advanced substantially over the past decades. Hantavax®, an inactivated orthohantavirus vaccine marketed in South Korea to prevent HFRS caused by Hantaan and Seoul viruses, remains among the only orthohantavirus vaccines licensed for human use, while several next-generation vaccine candidates are currently under development and evaluation in preclinical and early-phase clinical trials.4349 Despite these advances, effective countermeasures specifically targeting ANDV remain limited, highlighting an important preparedness gap for future outbreaks.In conclusion - Overall, current evidence does not support the conclusion that ANDV is imminently poised to emerge as a pandemic pathogen comparable to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Nevertheless, under favourable ecological and epidemiological conditions, localised ANDV outbreaks may increase in scale or geographic distribution, potentially posing broader regional public health challenges. These considerations underscore the importance of strengthening preparedness strategies to prevent the escalation of orthohantavirus outbreaks, particularly in under-resourced endemic regions of South America. Integrated ecological surveillance approaches, including climate-informed forecasting of rodent population dynamics,50 together with genomic epidemiological surveillance of ANDV and other clinically relevant orthohantaviruses, may improve early detection of spillover risk, characterise orthohantavirus diversity and evolutionary dynamics, and support timely public health responses. In addition, expanded availability of antiviral therapeutics, monoclonal antibodies, preventive vaccines, and rapid diagnostic platforms will be important for comprehensive orthohantavirus outbreak preparedness and response. These diagnostic platforms could include lateral-flow assays to detect orthohantavirus-specific IgM and IgG antibodies in symptomatic patients,51 as well as antigen-based tests for direct virus detection in both humans and reservoir hosts. REVIEWER #1The manuscript titled “Could Hantavirus Transmit the Next Pandemic?” presents a compelling and relevant discussion regarding the potential for hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) outbreaks. Prompted by the recent atypical HCPS outbreak associated with Andes orthohantavirus (ANDV) aboard the cruise ship M/V Hondius, the authors analyze this threat from virological, genomic, and eco-epidemiological perspectives. They convincingly argue that sustained person-to-person transmission would require highly specific—and currently unlikely—evolutionary conditions.The manuscript, from the abstract to the main text and references, is clear and well-structured. Notably, the authors present robust evidence that ANDV currently lacks the adaptive mutations necessary to drive person-to-person transmission in the manner observed with influenza viruses or SARS-CoV-2. This provides a timely and necessary clarification: although hantaviruses possess a trisegmented RNA genome capable of rapid mutation, reassortment and host adaptation, a large-scale epidemic remains highly unlikely. Finally, by advocating for an integrated global approach—combining genomic-epidemiological monitoring, rapid diagnostics, and accessible therapies—the authors highlight the precise surveillance strategies needed to contain localized HCPS outbreaks before they escalate into regional public health threats. Thus, in addition to adequately answering the title’s central question, the authors highlight the urgent global need for continuous, targeted surveillance—adopting a One Health approach—in areas endemic for SCPH, as well as for the accelerated development of effective diagnostics, specific therapies, and vaccines against HCPS.Minor comments: (i) standardized taxonomy — replace the word “hantavirus” with “orthohantavirus”, and (ii) in the graphical abstract : Oligoryzomys longicaudatus has been correctly italicized and change “exposure to aerosolised” to “inhalation of aerosolized.” REVIEWER #2This manuscript presents an interesting ecoevolutionary perspective into the outstanding question of Hantavirus’ pandemic potential. It has been discussed long before the Hondius outbreak that hantaviruses are worth being surveilled and studied to better understand if through evolution and expansion of host distributions and rodent-human contact interfaces, Hantaviruses could become the agents behind the next pandemic. The authors create a solid compendium of evidence regarding these scenarios and provide a grounded commentary on ANDV’s lack of pandemic potential at the moment, bringing a sobering message at a time when the lay public needs a better understanding of Hantaviruses.That being said, I would like to suggest some minor changes to enhance the flow of the manuscript:1. In the background section, there should be 2-3 sentences introducing the reader to the M/V Hondius situation. At the time of this review, the Hondius is not at the front page of the news anymore, and moreover, the manuscript should be timeless. For that reason, it would be good if the authors could include a section explaining the Hondius outbreak.2. Related to the first point, in lines 64-66, the authors dive right into discussing the “likelihood that the M/V Hondius ANDV cluster could progress into a sustained epidemic”. Before this section, there is no context of what the N/V Hondius ANDV cluster is.3. In lines 69-70, the authors mention that the sequences derived from the ANDV cluster have two synonymous mutations with respect to ANDV reference sequences from Argentina (1997 and 2018) and cite the Virological.org post by Dr. Gustavo Palacios. However, that is not what the post mentions; instead, the post describes two nonsynonymous mutations arising in the L segment between the first three sequences generated in South Africa, and they argue that this is a sign of a single spillover event as the origin of the index case. The original publication then mentions “98.76% and 98.75% based on the L segment, 98.71% and 98.68% on the M segment and 98.73% and 98.73% on the S segment”, these are with respect to the reference sequences from 1997 and 2018, which is more than two SNPs. Therefore, the authors should rectify the assertion of only two SNPs in the Hondius sequences, it would be evolutionarily impossible for an RNA virus to only accumulate two mutations in almost 30 years. full_text_sections.abstract: Despite concerns arising from a recent ship-associated outbreak on the M/V Hondius cruise, current evidence suggests that Andes virus (ANDV) poses a low pandemic risk. Nevertheless, viral evolution, ecological changes, and reservoir host dynamics could drive future emergence of ANDV, underscoring the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine preparedness.
full_text_sections.other: Could ANDV cause a future pandemic?Despite documented person-to-person transmission associated with the M/V Hondius cluster, current epidemiological and genomic evidence indicates that the likelihood of this outbreak progressing to sustained epidemic or pandemic transmission was exceedingly low. Prompt implementation of public health interventions, including quarantine measures and active surveillance of individuals aboard the vessel, facilitated the early identification and isolation of suspected cases. Furthermore, genomic analyses revealed remarkably limited viral diversity among sequenced cases from the M/V Hondius cluster, with identical S and M segment sequences and only two synonymous single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) detected within the L segment, one in case 5 and another in case 7. Importantly, no evidence of amino acid changes associated with enhanced transmissibility or sustained human-to-human spread was identified.18 In contrast, the outbreak sequences showed approximately 98.7% nucleotide identity across all three genome segments with ANDV sequences identified in Argentina in 1997 and 2018, indicating considerably greater divergence from these historical reference sequences.18 Furthermore, the reported positive cases fell within the incubation period of nine to 45 days for ANDV, suggesting that the cluster may have originated from a limited zoonotic exposure event, potentially followed by restricted secondary transmission, and is unlikely to develop into an epidemic or a pandemic event. However, given that ANDV has historically caused multiple outbreaks, it is important to highlight the conditions that could enable localised ANDV outbreaks to evolve and escalate into larger epidemics, and potentially, under exceptional circumstances, into a pandemic threat among human populations, as illustrated in Figure.Figure:Potential drivers of Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak escalation and pandemic emergence. ANDV is maintained in rodent reservoirs, primarily the long-tailed pygmy rice rat (Oligoryzomys longicaudatus), and is transmitted to humans through inhalation of aerosolised rodent excreta. Unlike other orthohantaviruses, ANDV can also undergo limited person-to-person transmission, although sustained community transmission has not been documented. The graphical abstract highlights three factors that could contribute to outbreak escalation: (i) viral evolution through mutation, reassortment, and host adaptation; (ii) environmental and ecological changes that increase rodent abundance and spillover risk; and (iii) expansion of reservoir host range through host switching and reservoir diversification. Under favourable ecological and evolutionary conditions, these processes could increase the scale, frequency, geographic distribution, or transmission potential of future outbreaks, underscoring the importance of continued surveillance, preparedness, and the development of effective diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines. Genetic variation arising during viral replication could theoretically influence viral fitness, host range, or transmission efficiency under selective pressures. Orthohantaviruses replicate using an error-prone RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), with evolutionary rates estimated at approximately 10−2-10−4 substitutions per site per year, consistent with rates reported for other RNA viruses.19 However, the relationship between genomic variation and altered transmissibility in ANDV remains incompletely understood, and no specific adaptive mutations have yet been conclusively associated with sustained human-to-human transmission.Previous studies have shown that ANDV strains from rodent and human hosts can produce markedly different outcomes in the Syrian hamster model.2021 Notably, a Chilean human isolate (CHI-7913), recovered from a fatal HPS case, acquired only a single non-synonymous mutation after 25 serial passages in hamsters and remained non-pathogenic, indicating relative genomic stability.20 In contrast, the rodent-derived isolate Chile-9717869 causes uniformly lethal disease despite differing by 23 amino acids from CHI-7913.21 Although these findings suggest a degree of genomic stability, they do not necessarily preclude adaptation. One possible explanation is that the CHI-7913 isolate had already undergone host-specific adaptation following zoonotic transmission to humans, thereby enhancing fitness in human cells while reducing replication efficiency and pathogenicity in the Syrian hamster model. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the pandemic risk of Andes virus (ANDV) following a recent ship-associated outbreak, addressing concerns about its potential to cause widespread transmission. The background highlights the need to evaluate whether documented person-to-person transmission could lead to sustained epidemic or pandemic spread.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed a ship-associated outbreak of ANDV, focusing on the M/V Hondius cruise. It included genomic analyses of sequenced cases and epidemiological data from the outbreak, with a sample size of seven confirmed cases.
analysis.methods: Genomic analyses were conducted on sequenced cases to assess viral diversity, while epidemiological data were used to evaluate the incubation period and transmission patterns. The study also examined the relationship between outbreak sequences and historical ANDV sequences from Argentina.
analysis.main_results: Genomic analyses revealed limited viral diversity among the sequenced cases, with identical S and M segment sequences and only two synonymous single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) detected within the L segment. No evidence of amino acid changes linked to enhanced transmissibility or sustained human-to-human spread was found. The outbreak sequences showed approximately 98.7% nucleotide identity with historical ANDV sequences from Argentina.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the likelihood of the outbreak progressing to sustained epidemic or pandemic transmission was exceedingly low, based on the limited viral diversity and absence of transmissibility-enhancing mutations. This finding highlights the importance of understanding conditions that could lead to outbreak escalation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine preparedness for ANDV, as well as emphasize the importance of monitoring conditions that might enable localized outbreaks to escalate into larger epidemics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single outbreak event, which may not fully represent the potential for broader transmission. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on genomic and epidemiological data from a specific incident rather than comprehensive long-term surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the pandemic risk of Andes virus (ANDV) following a recent ship-associated outbreak on the M/V Hondius cruise. It evaluates the likelihood of sustained transmission by analyzing genomic diversity and epidemiological data. The results indicate limited viral diversity and no evidence of transmissibility-enhancing mutations, suggesting a low probability of the outbreak evolving into a pandemic. The authors highlight the importance of monitoring conditions that could lead to outbreak escalation. The study's implications emphasize the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine preparedness for ANDV. However, the evidence is based on a single event, limiting its generalizability and suggesting a moderate confidence level in the findings.

elements_zh.methods: 对测序病例进行基因组分析以评估病毒多样性,同时使用流行病学数据评估潜伏期和 传播 模式。该研究还研究了 暴发 序列与阿根廷历史 ANDV 序列之间的关系。
elements_zh.main_results: 基因组分析显示,测序病例中的病毒多样性有限,S 和 M 片段序列相同,且在 L 片段内仅检测到两个同义单核苷酸多态性 (SNP)。没有发现与增强传播性或持续人际传播相关的氨基酸变化的证据。暴发 序列与来自阿根廷的历史 ANDV 序列显示出大约 98.7% 的核苷酸同一性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,基于有限的病毒多样性和缺乏传播性增强的 突变,暴发 发展为持续流行或大流行的 传播 的可能性极低。这一发现凸显了了解可能导致 暴发 升级的条件的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明需要改进 监测、诊断、治疗和 疫苗 针对 ANDV 的准备,并强调监测可能使局部 暴发 升级为更大流行病的情况的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它只关注单个 暴发 事件,这可能无法完全代表更广泛的 传播 的潜力。证据是中等的,因为它依赖于特定事件的基因组和流行病学数据,而不是全面的长期 监测。

analysis_zh.methods: 对测序病例进行基因组分析以评估病毒多样性,同时使用流行病学数据评估潜伏期和 传播 模式。该研究还研究了 暴发 序列与阿根廷历史 ANDV 序列之间的关系。
analysis_zh.main_results: 基因组分析显示,测序病例中的病毒多样性有限,S 和 M 片段序列相同,且在 L 片段内仅检测到两个同义单核苷酸多态性 (SNP)。没有发现与增强传播性或持续人际传播相关的氨基酸变化的证据。暴发 序列与来自阿根廷的历史 ANDV 序列显示出大约 98.7% 的核苷酸同一性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,基于有限的病毒多样性和缺乏传播性增强的 突变,暴发 发展为持续流行或大流行的 传播 的可能性极低。这一发现凸显了了解可能导致 暴发 升级的条件的重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明需要改进 监测、诊断、治疗和 疫苗 针对 ANDV 的准备,并强调监测可能使局部 暴发 升级为更大流行病的情况的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它只关注单个 暴发 事件,这可能无法完全代表更广泛的 传播 的潜力。证据是中等的,因为它依赖于特定事件的基因组和流行病学数据,而不是全面的长期 监测。
